flagged.evidence: The statement permits arbitrary T. With T=1, the tableau is 2x2, so there is no 2x3 window. The cited dependency lem-start-accept-and-transition-constraints-have-polynomial-size, step 1.2, says: “For each adjacent-row position and each illegal 2x3 pattern, add a clause forbidding that pattern.” Hence its move family is empty on this tableau. Let N reject epsilon in one step. The start and exactly-one constraints can be satisfied on row 0, and an accepting-state tag can be placed in row 1 to satisfy the accept disjunction; there is no transition clause preventing it. Thus psi_N,epsilon is satisfiable. But no accepting bounded computation tableau exists for N on epsilon, since def-bounded-computation-tableau requires every later row to be obtained by a legal transition and N rejects rather than accepts. The claimed biconditional is false.

Step 1.2 establishes only that the assignment “determines one symbol in every tableau cell,” then step 2.1 invokes [L3] to turn that array into a branch history. But def-bounded-computation-tableau defines a bounded computation tableau as an array whose row 0 is initial and whose “each later row is obtained from the previous row by one legal transition.” Its cited locality lemma likewise begins “Given: A bounded tableau T.” Therefore [L3] is stated only for an object already satisfying the computation-history condition; it cannot establish that an arbitrary cell-labeling extracted from a satisfying assignment has that condition. This circular use is the reverse implication of the lemma.

Step 2.1 says that an accepting bounded tableau “happens exactly when x in L.” The current tableau definition has no accepting-state stuttering convention: def-bounded-computation-tableau requires every later row to arise by a legal transition, while def-dtime-ntime-dspace-and-nspace defines the transition map only on Q minus {q_acc,q_rej}. Take a one-tape machine that accepts input 1 in one step but takes three steps on input 0. Any uniform polynomial time bound for length-one inputs has T at least 3. For x=1, x is in L, but after the accepting row there is no legal transition with which to fill the required remaining rows of the (T+1)x(T+1) tableau. Thus no accepting bounded tableau exists. A self-loop/padding convention or a final-row acceptance condition is required before this inference is valid.
